intent: You land on a wide safe ledge and the level is simply visible below you
A ledge just out of jumping range: the first thing the rope is for
A cache in plain sight one swing further out, so the reward reads as earned
The roof walkway is overhead and lit; you cannot reach it yet and you know it
Two shelves below the entry, so down is obviously an option too
One anchor hangs over the shaft mouth: the whole level is one swing away
Three jars on a shelf and no way to tell which is a sentinel
The chime that answers the question, if you shoot it before you touch anything
A side shelf under the gallery: the cautious way past the jars
A cache directly beneath the live jar, so the greedy line is the dangerous one
A lone anchor out over nothing, the reward for reading the room
A mural on the back wall of a narrow shelf: no room to back away from it
The shelf you land on if you flee the mural, deliberately just within one swing
A wide gallery floor, the first place in the west it is safe to stand and think
A ledge over the drop with a vent under it: the shortcut costs health
Two jars flanking the only route down, one of them alive
The bar that opens the kiln door, all the way across the level from it
One more shelf so the descent is a choice of lines, not a ladder
An anchor with nothing under it: your first swing that must land
A rope line staggered so the swing arcs are not a straight fall
The same again lower, tightening as the wall closes in
The last rope line above the water, wide enough to recover a bad swing
Broken shelves you can chain if you would rather climb than swing
A slab in mid-air with a cache on it, only reachable mid-swing
An anchor placed so the obvious swing carries you over the vent, not into it
A ledge that looks like a rest and has a mural on it
Stepping stones over the water gap, small enough to make you commit
The west waterline: shards in the shallows punish a missed landing
A high anchor that lets a confident player skip the whole descent
Where that skip lands you, right next to something that was waiting
The west lip of the shaft: the first place you can look straight down it
The east lip, visibly the same height, so the shaft reads as a crossing too
Anchors up the middle of the shaft: it is a way UP as much as down
An island in the middle of the shaft with the grate pin above it
A jar sits ON the island: the pin shot is taken from a compromised place
Ledges down the shaft's west wall for the careful route
And the east wall, offset, so the two routes cannot be taken at once
Mid-shaft lip with a vent on the wall at exactly swing height
Its opposite number, so the vent is passed on one side or the other
A slab low in the shaft holding a cache, in the vents' reach
The grate: shot open from the island far above, and you saw it happen
The slab under the grate, the only soft landing in the shaft's bottom
An assembler waits under the grate for whoever opens it
The last lip before the water, and an anchor to bail out with
Its twin, because a bail-out with one option is not a decision
Rope line strung above the water so a fall down the shaft is survivable
A cache tucked behind the shaft wall, visible only on the way down
The rope line continues east over the water toward the shrine
The first roof walkway, reachable only by a long swing from the entry side
The latch that opens the roof hatch, shot across the gap from here
The widest roof slab, and the only flat run up here
The roof hatch itself, opened from a walkway you had to reach first
The best cache in the level, on the roof, behind everything
Roof continues east, so the hatch is not the only thing up here
The last roof slab, overlooking the kiln stack
The roof anchor chain: four swings, no floor, one mistake is the whole drop
A broad kiln floor, hot at one end
A mural where the only standing room is beside a vent
A vent directly below a narrow ledge: staggered things fall into it
A shelf between two heats, wide enough to fight on and no wider
Kiln mouths in a rising line, the first place the route IS the hazard
The widest kiln tier, with a jar at the far end you will meet on the way back
A vent between you and that jar, which is the point
A lower tier, cooler, where you can see the whole stack you just crossed
The bottom of the stack, and an assembler between you and the east wall
The east high shelf with a jar guarding a cache
A shelf you reach by rope only, holding nothing: a lesson about greed
The mural on that empty shelf, which is what it was really holding
A shelf under the empty one, so fleeing downward is possible
Low east shelf, with the kiln cache behind a vent
The winch that opens the west vault, an entire level away from the vault
A mural directly behind the winch: you pull it with your back turned
The tier the winch fight spills onto
The kiln door, opened by a bar back in the west galleries
Past the kiln door: a shrine, because the deep east is a long way from anywhere
Rope out over the deep east water
Shards under the east rope line, so a missed swing over the water still costs you
An assembler in the last stretch of water before the way out
A jar on the high east shelf, positioned to emerge behind you at the cache
One anchor at the far east edge so the wall is never a dead end
And the corner, which would otherwise be the one place you could strand yourself
The way on to Burial Works, at the deep east end
The cistern floor proper, broken so the water is always near
A supplicant on a slab above the water, still holding her token
An assembler between you and her, closer to her than to you
The shrine beside her, so you can save and try again
The offering cache at her feet: taking it is not the same as protecting her
The anchor you would naturally rope to cross -- it is over HER slab
West floor, with the first water gap immediately after it
A floor island with shards on both approaches
Another island, smaller, so crossing the floor is its own traversal problem
The narrowest island, right under the shaft, where falls land
East floor begins, with an assembler already up
The last floor run to the exit, deliberately clear: you have earned it
The west vault door, opened by the winch across the level
The vault opens on a cache and nothing else, so the winch was worth crossing the level for
An island shelf so the east water is crossable without the rope
Rope between the west wing and the shaft, so the two halves are one place
Rope between the shaft and the kiln stack, same reason
And lower, so the crossing is possible at more than one height
The lowest crossing between the two halves, taken at water level where a fall is short
Rope back up to the entry, so the level is never one-way
